name: Mini Tiffin
steps: Soak idli rice, urad dal and fenugreek for 5 hours, grind with enough of the measured water to a smooth thick batter, and ferment overnight until risen. Add half the salt; reserve half the batter for mini idlis and thin the rest slightly for dosas.
Oil mini-idli moulds, fill them three-quarters with batter and steam over boiling water for 8–10 minutes. Rest briefly and unmould; make about twelve mini idlis.

For pongal, rinse short-grain rice and moong dal, then simmer with about 360 ml of the measured water until very soft, 20–25 minutes. Heat 25 g ghee, toast cumin and crushed pepper, then fold into the soft rice-dal mixture with a pinch of salt.

For kesari, roast semolina in 20 g ghee until fragrant. Bring 250 ml of the measured water with sugar to a boil, add roasted semolina slowly while stirring, and cook until thick and glossy. Fry cashews in 10 g ghee and scatter on top.
Heat a flat griddle and make four small dosas from the reserved batter, using the measured oil around the edges; cook until lightly crisp and golden. Warm the prepared sambar.

Arrange three mini idlis, one small dosa, a spoonful of pongal and a separate spoonful of sweet kesari on each of four plates. Add coconut chutney and sambar alongside so the sweet portion stays distinct.
tips: Keep the sweet kesari in its own section so it does not soak up sambar.
passiveTime: Soak rice and urad dal for 5 hours, then ferment the batter overnight.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
